threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local document-processing engine exposed through Rust APIs, a native CLI, Python bindings/CLI, WebAssembly packages and a Python stdio MCP server. It consumes untrusted document/archive/XML/media bytes and edit plans, returns transformed documents, views and renderings, and optionally publishes local files. Native CLI I/O has ambient filesystem authority; MCP document I/O uses a held directory capability. Native rendering also accesses ambient font resources and a persistent font index. Explicit self-update downloads and installs GitHub release binaries. Maintainer release workflows publish distributable artifacts. Evidence: src/lib.rs:86; Cargo.toml:83; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:37; jubarte-wasm/cli/package.json:35; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:72; src/publication.rs:155; src/publication.rs:211; src/convert/font.rs:3100; src/update.rs:198; .github/workflows/release.yml:364.
assets: Confidential document text, comments, revisions, embedded media and resulting DOCX/PDF/PNG/report artifacts. MCP edit output includes clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json beneath the selected out_dir: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:195.

Host filesystem contents and existing outputs. MCP grants a directory capability once; CLI publication explicitly grants ambient local access: src/publication.rs:155; src/publication.rs:162; src/publication.rs:175; src/publication.rs:211.

Host memory and CPU handling untrusted packages. Default admission caps compressed bytes at 64 MiB, entries at 10,000, individual inflated parts at 64 MiB, total inflation at 256 MiB and XML depth at 256. Comparison defaults are materially larger: 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB total: src/admission.rs:63; src/admission.rs:87.

Installed executable integrity, GitHub release artifacts, release signing authority and package publication authority: src/update.rs:198; src/update.rs:245; .github/workflows/release.yml:263; .github/workflows/release.yml:358; scripts/release.sh:919; scripts/release.sh:935; scripts/release.sh:952; scripts/release.sh:1069.

Native renderer font files and persistent index. Font search uses configured/platform directories; default index is beside the fonts directory, not inside it, and records font file paths consumed on later conversions: src/convert/font.rs:2637; src/convert/font.rs:3100; src/convert/font.rs:3165.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document suppliers cross into in-process ZIP/XML/media parsing. Admission applies configured byte/count/depth budgets and bounded inflated reads; shared archive opening applies zip_defects before use. Direct unchecked archive opening is retained for diagnostic inspection: src/admission.rs:439; src/admission.rs:531; src/opc/archive.rs:20; src/opc/archive.rs:42.

Public checked XML parsing validates before DOM construction; permissive parse_xdocument remains a different API whose caller must establish appropriate trust/admission. Tag defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte qualified attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:49; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:119; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

MCP caller arguments cross into host document reads and publication. Python resolves paths for early diagnostics, while native _OutputRoot performs capability-relative read/publish using the directory held by publication::OutputRoot. Tool annotations are hints to the host, not an approval or per-tool authorization mechanism: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:72; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:84; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1254; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1260; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1265; docs/adoption/mcp.md:39.

Native CLI and Python CLI callers already possess ambient local path authority. CLI publication uses publish_paths; Python CLI reads caller-specified paths. Their authority must not be conflated with the MCP root capability: src/publication.rs:211; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:61; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73.

Rendering crosses from document-requested font families into ambient platform/configured font resources and cache writes. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR controls the font folder; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX independently overrides or disables the index; absent override, the index is parent(font-folder)/font-index.tsv. These operations use std::fs rather than MCP OutputRoot: src/convert/font.rs:2637; src/convert/font.rs:3100; src/convert/font.rs:3165; src/convert/font.rs:3213.

Explicit updater crosses from GitHub release authority into installed executable replacement. It selects a platform-specific archive/member, requests SHA256SUMS.txt verification and checks the extracted binary is a regular file. Signature verification is conditional, and this source has RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None: src/update.rs:25; src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; src/update.rs:91; src/update.rs:104; src/update.rs:198; src/update.rs:245; src/update.rs:308.

Tag-triggered CI builds cross into a privileged release job with contents:write. Only the signing step receives ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, which is decoded into ephemeral runner files; the publication step receives GITHUB_TOKEN and uploads dist/* to the current repository release: .github/workflows/release.yml:15; .github/workflows/release.yml:20; .github/workflows/release.yml:230; .github/workflows/release.yml:234; .github/workflows/release.yml:263; .github/workflows/release.yml:278; .github/workflows/release.yml:285; .github/workflows/release.yml:358; .github/workflows/release.yml:364.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control input package structures, XML, media, embedded fonts and document content without already controlling the host filesystem, operator environment or release infrastructure: src/admission.rs:439; src/opc/archive.rs:42; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:134.

An MCP client can supply tool arguments, document paths, edit plans, output directories and explicit overwrite flags within the granted root; it does not thereby receive ambient CLI authority. The server is started on stdio, without a network listener: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:381.

An actor able to replace release archives and their adjacent checksum file has meaningful influence over checksum-only updater installations. Such release-write authority is a separate prerequisite, not an ordinary document supplier capability: src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; src/update.rs:245; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59.
securityObjectives: Reject malformed or over-budget untrusted packages before expensive document processing; retain host-enforced process limits because admission budgets do not establish a universal CPU/memory bound: src/admission.rs:63; src/admission.rs:87; src/admission.rs:439; src/admission.rs:531.

Confine MCP document reads/publication to the held root, preserve existing outputs unless replacement is explicitly authorized, and do not treat Python prechecks as the actual I/O authorization: src/publication.rs:155; src/publication.rs:162; src/publication.rs:175; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:101.

Stage all output bytes before publishing and expose accurate partial-commit state if later commits fail. Publication is atomic per file, not across an output set: src/publication.rs:83; src/publication.rs:123.

Keep update execution explicit and preserve executable integrity through release selection, checksums, configured signature policy and extracted-file type verification: src/update.rs:186; src/update.rs:198; src/update.rs:245; src/update.rs:255; src/update.rs:308.

Keep release signing material confined to the signing step and distinguish artifact-build read permissions from release-publication write permissions: .github/workflows/release.yml:20; .github/workflows/release.yml:234; .github/workflows/release.yml:263; .github/workflows/release.yml:278.
assumptions: No user deployment context or external authoritative threat model was supplied. This is a source-backed architecture map, not completed security-audit coverage or proof of deployment isolation.

MCP documentation says outputs are under root, but native rendering also writes an ambient font index outside root under default platform configurations. The document-output capability is established; a claim that the whole renderer process touches only root is not: docs/adoption/mcp.md:61; docs/adoption/mcp.md:69; src/convert/font.rs:3100; src/convert/font.rs:3213.

Signature support is implemented but not enabled by this source's empty key list and unset first-signed version. Documentation explicitly describes this staged checksum-only state; do not infer mandatory signatures from feature support: src/update.rs:44; src/update.rs:48; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69.

Native rendering configuration and environment are operator-owned unless a particular embedding exposes them. Documents do not automatically gain control of JUBARTE_FONT_DIR or JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX: src/convert/font.rs:2637; src/convert/font.rs:3100.

Browser/Node WebAssembly and native bindings must retain separate runtime authority assumptions. The npm CLI is a Node entrypoint backed by jubarte-wasm, while Python uses native Rust with the shared CLI feature and disables engine default features: jubarte-wasm/cli/package.json:35; jubarte-wasm/cli/package.json:46; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:37.

Registry credentials, GitHub repository permissions, host filesystem ACLs and actual signing-secret availability are deployment prerequisites not verified by offline source inspection: .github/workflows/release.yml:263; .github/workflows/release.yml:358; scripts/release.sh:919; scripts/release.sh:935; scripts/release.sh:1069.

findings.title: Rendering auxiliary XML under a different extension bypasses the depth limit
findings.summary: A crafted DOCX can point a styles, theme, note, comment or header/footer relationship at deeply nested XML stored under a non-XML extension. Admission skips that part's XML policy, but rendering parses it recursively, allowing a small document to exhaust the host stack and terminate the process.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reliably reach unbounded recursion during ordinary rendering and terminate the containing CLI, Python worker or WASM instance. Impact is availability; no confidentiality or code-execution claim. Rendering the malicious document is required.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation limits impact to one worker; a shared rendering host increases availability impact. Applying active XML limits to every relationship-selected XML consumer removes the bypass.

confidence.rationale: Parent source trace confirms extension-only admission, unrestricted internal relationship target selection and unchecked recursive parsing. No runtime crash was executed; exact failing depth depends on stack/runtime.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion through XML admission bypass

codeEvidence.label: Rendering admits before loading auxiliary parts
codeEvidence.explanation: The caller-controlled package is admitted and normalized, then its parts are loaded; the auxiliary parser assumes the earlier admission covered them.

codeEvidence.label: XML policy selected by filename suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: A styles.bin/theme.bin part enters the byte-only branch, so its XML nesting and tag policy are not checked. The later special case at 556-569 covers only the main document.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship type selects an arbitrary internal part name
codeEvidence.explanation: The document relationship controls the path. Rejecting External prevents fetching but imposes no XML-extension or content-depth validation.

codeEvidence.label: Theme bytes reach the permissive DOM parser
codeEvidence.explanation: Relationship-selected attacker bytes are decoded and parsed without the checked XML API; styles similarly loads at 3480 and parses at 3497.

codeEvidence.label: Every nested element consumes another stack frame
codeEvidence.explanation: The permissive parser recurses without a depth budget. A ~700 KiB auxiliary part containing 100000 nested tags is well within byte limits and can exhaust the host stack.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` chooses XML policy by `.xml`/`.rels` suffix and separately checks only the main document. Rendering locates auxiliary XML by relationship type, which permits arbitrary internal filenames, then uses `parse_xdocument()` without validation. Thus an attacker can store a deeply nested theme or stylesheet in a `.bin` part and reach `Parser::parse_element()` recursion despite the configured depth of 256.

findings.remediation: Enforce active XML limits before DOM construction for every relationship-selected XML part, regardless of filename. Resolve relevant relationship/content-type XML parts during admission and use checked, depth-bounded parsing at auxiliary consumers; do not rely on extensions as the parser trust boundary.

counterEvidence: Ordinary .xml/.rels parts are checked for depth and tag budgets; the main document is checked even under another extension.
Archive byte/count/CRC/extent controls still apply, but a deeply nested auxiliary XML can fit below them.
The public permissive XML API documents caller obligations; the affected product renderer is the unchecked internal consumer. CommentFamily::load separately validates and is not included.
limitations: No application execution or runtime stack-overflow reproduction performed.
Additional relationship-selected consumers are being reconciled; current finding anchors prove theme and styles.
validation.method: Independent parent static source and countercontrol review
validation.summary: A normal Transitional DOCX with a theme/styles relationship to a `.bin` XML part passes the extension filter; normalization leaves the part unchanged (strict_translation.rs:809-831), PartFs only bounds inflation (opc/mod.rs:282-351), and load_theme/load_stylesheet parses its bytes recursively. The special main-part depth check does not cover it.

dataflow.summary: DOCX relationship target -> filename-only admission bypass -> PartFs part_string -> load_theme/load_stylesheet -> unchecked DOM recursion -> process stack exhaustion
dataflow.source: Document supplier controls package names, relationships and auxiliary XML bytes.
dataflow.outcome: Rendering process or WASM instance terminates from stack exhaustion.

reachability.summary: Public rendering APIs call with_layout on caller-provided bytes. No operator configuration or prior filesystem access is needed; a host must choose to render the supplied document.
preconditions: Victim processes attacker-supplied DOCX with rendering/layout.

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid DOCX with an internal theme/styles relationship targeting a non-.xml/.rels part, put tens of thousands of nested elements there, and request PDF/PNG/layout rendering.

remediationTests: Use renamed styles/theme parts with depth 257 and 100000 and assert typed refusal before DOM construction.
Cover renamed comments, notes, headers and footers and preserve valid shallow arbitrary-name parts.
Run equivalent public Rust, Python and WASM rendering inputs with the active limit configuration.

findings.title: Rendering a tiny table can allocate billions of columns
findings.summary: DOCX `gridSpan`, `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` values become unbounded layout counts. A one-cell document can request approximately 16 GiB for a single column vector and exhaust or abort rendering.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document input readily causes availability loss in ordinary rendering. No memory corruption or code execution is claimed; process limits contain shared-host effects.
severity.changeConditions: A total-column budget enforced before all grid-sized allocations removes this path; dedicated worker limits reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent source trace confirms numeric input -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> direct allocation. No runtime OOM was executed.

taxonomy.category: Excessive allocation from untrusted table dimensions

codeEvidence.label: Document tables enter layout
codeEvidence.explanation: Main-story table nodes from the supplied document enter table_block.

codeEvidence.label: gridSpan lacks an upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker numeric span becomes usize with only minimum one.

codeEvidence.label: Skipped columns lack an upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: gridBefore/After accepts positive usize stored as RawCell.colspan at 14379.

codeEvidence.label: Spans directly size column allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Unchecked effective occupancy directly sizes f32 vectors, allowing a 16GiB allocation from one large count.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span()` parses gridSpan as usize with only minimum one; `row_grid_skip()` likewise accepts arbitrary positive gridBefore/gridAfter. These enter RawCell.colspan. `table_block()` sums spans into occupancy and uses it for vec allocation/resize without checked cumulative bounds or a rendering column budget.

findings.remediation: Enforce a conservative total-column budget for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before RawCell or vector creation. Use checked sums and return a typed conversion refusal on excess; apply the bound to every preference/merge allocation.

counterEvidence: ZIP/XML syntax and byte budgets remain effective.
PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS applies after layout; PDF and render reports also lay out tables.
Caller process limits contain the worker but do not bound this tiny-input allocation.
limitations: No product code or runtime OOM reproduction executed.
validation.summary: A shallow, normally admitted one-cell table with gridSpan 4294967295 reaches occupancy unchanged, causing cols.resize or vec![each; occupancy] to request 4294967295 f32 values. Row skips enter the same mechanism. Byte/depth admission imposes no bound on numeric magnitude.

dataflow.summary: Document numeric spans -> usize -> RawCell.colspan -> summed occupancy -> grid-sized vectors
dataflow.sink: table_block column allocation and preference/merge vectors
dataflow.outcome: Memory exhaustion/allocation failure terminates the worker.

reachability.summary: Public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs layout attacker-provided document tables; no operator configuration or filesystem mutation is needed.

attackPath.summary: Supply DOCX containing <w:gridSpan w:val="4294967295"/> in a one-cell table, then request rendering. Equivalent row gridBefore/gridAfter counts reach the same allocation.

remediationTests: Excessive individual and cumulative spans/skips must refuse with bounded work.
Cover count overflow and 32-bit WASM.
Keep valid merged/skipped-column rendering.

findings.title: A tiny HTML table can generate billions of XML elements during rendering
findings.summary: An HTML/MHT altChunk cell's unbounded colspan controls a loop generating Word grid columns. A short related chunk can exhaust CPU and memory before DOM construction or rendering limits apply.

severity.rationale: A supplier-controlled document can terminate its rendering host using a small package without special configuration. Availability impact is confined by worker resource isolation; no execution or external fetch is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: Bound effective columns and generated WML work/bytes before expansion; isolated worker limits contain host-wide effects.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified with_layout -> expand -> html_to_wml -> parsed colspan -> unbounded append loop. Runtime exhaustion was not executed.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering expands package-local HTML
codeEvidence.explanation: The admitted package's related HTML/MHT is expanded before the main DOM parse.

codeEvidence.label: Chunk text is converted into WML
codeEvidence.explanation: Related chunk bytes are decoded and passed to the HTML-to-WML builder.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded HTML colspan count
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker colspan is parsed as usize with only a minimum.

codeEvidence.label: One XML grid element emitted per claimed column
codeEvidence.explanation: The sum of input spans controls an unbounded append loop, with no generated-byte/work limit.

rootCause.summary: Rendering expands related HTML/MHT after package admission. `Builder::start()` accepts any positive usize colspan. `end_table()` sums spans, then appends one gridCol element for every claimed column without limiting generated bytes or work. The bounded original chunk therefore expands into an unbounded intermediate WML string.

findings.remediation: Cap HTML colspan and total effective table columns using checked arithmetic before expansion. Enforce a generated-WML byte/work budget and return a conversion refusal rather than partially generating an excessive chunk.

counterEvidence: Chunk bytes are package-local, without a filesystem or network fetch.
Input budgets bound original archive/XML bytes rather than generated markup.
Page pixel limits and caller process limits do not bound this earlier work.
Separate from native WML grid-vector allocation: this path must be stopped in HTML expansion itself.
limitations: No application execution or runtime exhaustion test performed.
validation.summary: A single HTML cell with colspan4294967295 makes cols4294967295 and the loop writes over85GB of grid-column markup. Expansion precedes DOM parsing, so even later table-vector bounds would not address this generator sink.

dataflow.summary: DOCX altChunk relationship -> chunk_html -> html_to_wml -> usize colspan -> effective cols -> repeated gridCol append

reachability.summary: Normal with_layout callers expand any referenced altChunk from the supplied package before constructing the main DOM.
preconditions: Victim renders a document containing the supplied chunk.

Include a related HTML/MHT altChunk with
x
and request rendering.

Cover malformed spans, overflow and nested tables.
Preserve valid small HTML tables.

findings.title: Large page coordinates make border rendering loop without progress
findings.summary: Finite page dimensions and margins from DOCX can place a dotted border at coordinates where its f32 increment rounds to zero. Rendering then loops indefinitely while appending drawing operations, exhausting memory.

severity.rationale: Ordinary document rendering crosses from supplier-controlled section geometry to a nonterminating loop; availability is affected without host configuration. CPU/memory limits contain the worker but still permit denial of service.
severity.changeConditions: Reject excessive geometry, compute bounded integer segment counts and enforce operation budgets; isolation reduces shared-host consequences.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirmed unbounded geometry, text-relative endpoints, f32 step and per-iteration push. At1e9 float spacing exceeds1, proving nonprogress. No runtime hang executed.

codeEvidence.label: Page and margins accept unbounded lengths
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker page width and left margin become f32 coordinates without a maximum.

codeEvidence.label: Border widths and style determine the step
codeEvidence.explanation: sz=1 maps to 0.24pt; dotted style later clamps on/off to0.5 each.

codeEvidence.label: Text-relative border uses large margins
codeEvidence.explanation: Default text-relative border places left endpoint at the unbounded margin.

codeEvidence.label: Float loop lacks progress and operation budget
codeEvidence.explanation: At p=1e9, f32 p+1 equals p; condition remains true and each iteration adds an operation.

codeEvidence.label: Each iteration appends a drawing operation
codeEvidence.explanation: Even zero-length coordinate progress pushes a minimum-width FillRect, exhausting memory.

rootCause.summary: `apply_sect_pr()` accepts unbounded f32 page dimensions and margins. A text-relative border starts at that margin. Dotted-border painting clamps on/off intervals to0.5 each, then repeatedly adds1 to the f32 position. At a large finite coordinate this addition cannot change the value; the while condition remains true and each iteration pushes another FillRect.

findings.remediation: Validate finite, reasonable page/margin/border geometry before layout. Use a bounded integer segment count instead of open-ended float accumulation, enforce a maximum border-operation budget, and explicitly refuse any step that cannot advance.

counterEvidence: All trigger numbers are finite; a NaN/infinity-only check would not fix the problem.
word_pgsz_pt only adjusts two A4 sizes and otherwise returns the supplied size.
MAX_PAGE_PIXELS applies after this layout loop, and PDF/render reports reach it too.
Process limits can kill the worker, not make the loop terminate.
limitations: No product execution, hang or allocation-failure reproduction performed.
validation.method: Independent parent static source and arithmetic review
validation.summary: pgSz width40000000000twips gives2e9pt; pgMar left20000000000 gives1e9pt. A top dotted border sz1 space0 starts at1e9 and ends near2e9. Its1pt total increment is smaller than the f32 representable spacing, so p never advances. Layout::new calls chrome/paint_pg_borders before PDF/PNG emission.

dataflow.summary: DOCX pgSz/pgMar/pgBorders -> unbounded f32 PageSetup -> border endpoints -> p+=on+off rounds to p -> endless FillRect accumulation
dataflow.source: Supplier-controlled section geometry and border style

findings.title: npm plan recording follows a predictable staging symlink
findings.summary: When recording plan operations, the npm CLI writes to a basename/PID staging path without exclusive creation. A local attacker who can create entries in that directory can redirect the write to an unrelated file writable by the CLI user.

severity.rationale: This is a local, conditional file-integrity failure: exploitation needs attacker write access to the plan directory and prediction/observation of the CLI PID. The target must be writable by the victim. These constrained prerequisites lower likelihood.
severity.changeConditions: A workflow routinely recording plans in a directory writable by less-trusted users increases likelihood. An exclusive regular staging file in a private unpredictable directory removes the link-following path.

confidence.rationale: Source directly constructs predictable partial name, calls default fs.writeFileSync and only then renames. No exclusive/no-follow protection applies; no runtime filesystem manipulation was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Plan recording route
codeEvidence.explanation: A normal edit with plan plus operation flags enters recordPlan.

codeEvidence.label: Predictable staging path is followed by default write
codeEvidence.explanation: Directory attacker can plant the basename/PID partial as symlink; writeFileSync follows it and truncates referent before rename.

rootCause.summary: `runEdit()` routes plan-plus-operation flags to `recordPlan()`. It derives the temporary pathname solely from target basename and process PID and calls `fs.writeFileSync()` with default truncating write semantics. A preexisting symlink at that pathname is followed, modifying its referent before `renameSync()` can publish the plan. Resolving the intended plan target does not validate the separate staging entry.

findings.remediation: Create an unpredictable private staging directory next to the plan and open the staged regular file exclusively. Write through its held descriptor and rename only that file. At minimum refuse every preexisting staging entry using exclusive creation rather than default truncating writes.

counterEvidence: Requires local shared-directory write and a predictable PID; no extra OS file permissions are obtained.
Intentional symlink resolution for the operator-selected plan is separate from the attacker-selected staging link.
Native Rust publication uses private UUID staging/exclusive creation but the npm path does not call it.
Dry-run skips the write.
limitations: No symlink creation or product execution was performed.
No actual shared-directory deployment was supplied; this prerequisite remains conditional.
validation.summary: No filesystem check or exclusive open lies between partial-name construction and writeFileSync. Precreation of that name can select a different victim-writable file outside the plan directory. Subsequent rename moves the staging link, after the referent has already been overwritten.

dataflow.summary: Plan basename/PID -> attacker-controlled staging directory entry -> default writeFileSync -> external referent truncation/write -> rename
dataflow.source: Local attacker controls staging pathname entry
dataflow.outcome: Unrelated victim-writable file overwritten with plan JSON.

reachability.summary: The npm CLI exposes recordPlan through normal edit --plan plus operations. A separate local directory writer is required; document bytes alone cannot choose the staging link.
reachability.attacker: Less-trusted local user with plan-directory write access
preconditions: Victim records a plan in an attacker-writable directory.
Attacker predicts/observes PID and can create a staging symlink.
Referent is writable by victim process.

attackPath.summary: In a plan directory writable by the attacker, precreate the predictable partial name as a symlink to a victim-writable external file; wait for the victim to record operations into that plan.

remediationTests: Preexisting partial symlink must cause refusal without changing its referent.
Concurrent staging-name collisions must fail safely.
Valid plan recording and dry-run behavior remain correct.

findings.title: Redaction succeeds while UTF-16 XML retains the removed text
findings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported UTF-16 auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its leak checker decodes XML only as UTF-8 and misses the retained copy.

severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.
severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified UTF16 admission, raw part retention/output, XML-only lossy UTF8 branch and success gate. Baseline validation allows unchanged auxiliary issues. No product execution was performed.

taxonomy.category: Incomplete removal of sensitive document information

codeEvidence.label: Admission supports UTF16 XML
codeEvidence.explanation: Supported BOM-marked UTF16 parts enter the package, including customXml.

codeEvidence.label: XML branch uses lossy UTF8 only
codeEvidence.explanation: Raw UTF16 matching is confined to the other branch; UTF16 XML goes to semantic scanning as NUL-interleaved text.

codeEvidence.label: No leak hits permits output
codeEvidence.explanation: Both output leak searches must find the secret to refuse; no hits advances as success.

codeEvidence.label: Ordinary parts retain raw bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: Non-relationship XML is stored as original bytes, including unmodified UTF16 customXml.

codeEvidence.label: Remaining bytes are serialized unchanged
codeEvidence.explanation: The hidden secret-bearing auxiliary bytes remain readable in the outgoing ZIP.

rootCause.summary: Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes.

findings.remediation: Decode every XML part with the same BOM-aware policy as admission before semantic leak scanning. Fail closed on unsupported/undecodable representations and retain raw UTF8 and both UTF16 byte-order checks as defense in depth. Use the same decoding across leak checks and package validation.

counterEvidence: Unreadable archives/entries and inflation-budget failures correctly refuse redaction.
UTF8 XML entities and Word text split across runs are handled.
UTF16 raw matching exists for non-XML parts only.
Normal redaction outcome diagnostics avoid repeating the secret.
limitations: No product-generated trigger or runtime redaction test executed.
Disclosure requires the resulting package to be shared or inspected by another party.
validation.method: Independent parent static encoding, serialization and gate review
validation.summary: An ordinary multi-character secret in BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml survives raw package storage and serialization. UTF8-lossy decoding produces replacement/NUL-interleaved text; xml_holds either has no root and uses a UTF8 substring check or cannot match decoded ordinary text. Both final artifacts are checked with that same routine. Existing malformed-XML validation findings are baseline, not automatically introduced failures.

dataflow.summary: Supported UTF16 auxiliary XML -> unchanged PartFs bytes -> UTF8-lossy leak scan misses copy -> redaction success -> raw secret-bearing part serialized
dataflow.sink: Redaction leak certification and outgoing ZIP parts
dataflow.outcome: Recipient can recover the supposedly removed text.

preconditions: Input contains duplicate text in BOM UTF16 auxiliary XML.
User redacts visible text and distributes the output.

attackPath.summary: Supply a document with a visible secret and a duplicate in UTF16 customXml. The recipient redacts the visible occurrence and shares the successful output; the receiver reads the retained auxiliary copy.

remediationTests: Redact visible body text while UTF16LE and UTF16BE customXml retains the same text; require REDACTION_LEAK.
Cover XML entities, split runs and encoding errors.
A document with no remaining copy must still redact successfully.

findings.title: Metadata scrub leaves property parts under alternate names
findings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success.

severity.rationale: The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.
severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirmed fixed path constants, exact-path loads, conditional custom cleanup, arbitrary package relationship preservation and validation-based success. No Word or application execution performed.

taxonomy.category: Incomplete removal of sensitive document metadata

codeEvidence.label: Only three conventional property names
codeEvidence.explanation: Property removal is keyed to fixed constants rather than package relationship targets.

codeEvidence.label: Selected docprops scrub invokes fixed-path mutator
codeEvidence.explanation: The enabled option runs scrub_properties, then returns successfully if validation has no new finding.

codeEvidence.label: Properties scrub resolves fixed paths only
codeEvidence.explanation: Alternate core/app/custom property targets are left intact; custom cleanup only runs when the conventional file exists.

codeEvidence.label: Package relations and raw property bytes retained
codeEvidence.explanation: Actual relationships and arbitrary ordinary part names are loaded without restricting metadata to conventional paths.

rootCause.summary: `scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition.

findings.remediation: Discover core, extended and custom property parts through package relationship types and resolved targets, with content-type-aware handling where needed. Remove every selected part/field and all corresponding relationships/content-type records, and verify the privacy postcondition rather than silently skipping unsupported representations.

counterEvidence: Conventional property files are scrubbed and conventional custom properties get part/relationship/content-type cleanup.
The operation intentionally preserves title/subject/application and revision dates; those are outside this finding.
Existing tests use conventional metadata names and do not establish alternate-target handling.
limitations: No runtime or Word compatibility reproduction executed.
Actual confidentiality impact depends on retained values and subsequent document distribution.
validation.method: Independent parent static metadata discovery/mutation/output review
validation.summary: A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.

dataflow.summary: Alternate property relationship/part -> PartFs preserves actual name -> fixed-path scrub misses it -> validation unchanged -> raw property part remains in output
dataflow.source: Supplier-controlled property relationship targets and metadata
dataflow.sink: scrub_properties incomplete discovery and outgoing package serialization
dataflow.outcome: Document receiver reads supposedly removed metadata.

reachability.summary: Default ScrubOptions enables docprops. The public scrub API opens package relationships without constraining property filenames; no operator configuration is required.
reachability.attacker: Untrusted document supplier or outgoing document recipient
preconditions: Metadata uses an alternate package target.
User scrubs before distributing the resulting document.

attackPath.summary: Provide a document whose package property relationship targets an alternate-named part containing identifying data; recipient runs default/docprops scrub and distributes the successful result.

remediationTests: Use alternate core/app/custom filenames and case variants with valid relationships/content types.
Confirm selected fields/parts are absent and references coherent afterward.
Keep intentional title/subject/application retention.

findings.title: A DTD literal bypasses package XML depth checks
findings.summary: Package admission accepts a DOCTYPE as one ignored event, while the subsequent permissive DOM parser skips it only through the first `>`. Markup remaining inside a quoted DTD literal is then parsed as nested elements, bypassing the depth budget and exhausting the host stack.

severity.rationale: A small ordinary-named document part can cause process stack exhaustion through public document processing. Impact is availability without privileged configuration; no external entity fetch or code execution is asserted.
severity.changeConditions: Rejecting DTD declarations at package admission and enforcing parser depth makes the representations agree. Isolated workers reduce shared-host impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent traced both parser interpretations and checked the locked quick-xml0.42 DTD parser's quote-sensitive skip. No runtime stack exhaustion was executed; the exact crash depth depends on runtime stack size.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion from XML parser disagreement

codeEvidence.label: Package XML scanner ignores non-element events
codeEvidence.explanation: DOCTYPE is neither rejected nor interpreted; only actual Start/Empty events contribute to depth.

codeEvidence.label: DOM skip stops at the first closing angle bracket
codeEvidence.explanation: The first > can occur inside an entity literal; remaining literal markup is then treated as real elements.

codeEvidence.label: Nested literal markup consumes the call stack
codeEvidence.explanation: The permissive parser recursively processes elements without a depth guard.

codeEvidence.label: Checked XML API rejects DTD declarations
codeEvidence.explanation: The independent checked parser already has a DTD refusal absent from package admission.

codeEvidence.label: Normal rendering uses package gate then permissive DOM
codeEvidence.explanation: The main XML reaches unchecked DOM parsing after the streaming admission gate.

rootCause.summary: `check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission.

findings.remediation: Reject DocType events in package admission consistently with validate_xml, and enforce depth within DOM parsing or use the checked API with active limits before every consumer. If declarations must be tolerated, parse their full quoted/internal-subset grammar instead of stopping at the first `>`.

counterEvidence: Ordinary nested XML elements are depth-checked.
try_parse_xdocument/validate_xml reject DTD at xmllinq/parse.rs:954, but product rendering uses admission then the permissive parser.
No entity expansion or external resource resolution is needed.
Input byte limits and process limits still constrain/isolate overall effects.
limitations: No product execution or runtime crash reproduction performed.
Other callers using checked XML parsing are protected and are not claimed affected.
validation.method: Independent parent static parser-differential review including locked dependency source
validation.summary: A valid internal entity declaration can contain a long literal with nested tag text without using the entity. quick-xml0.42 consumes the entire declaration as DocType (cached src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265), so package depth remains shallow. The DOM skip ends at the literal's first tag terminator and immediately enters recursion over the remaining literal. Normal rendering parses before it can reject the phantom root. This is independent of non-XML filenames.

dataflow.summary: Document DOCTYPE literal -> streaming DocType ignored by admission -> first-> declaration skip -> literal tags interpreted as elements -> unbounded recursion

reachability.summary: Public rendering admits caller bytes with check_xml_depth and later calls permissive parse_xdocument on the same main XML. A `.bin` alias or operator setting is unnecessary.
preconditions: Victim processes attacker-supplied package through an affected unchecked DOM consumer.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX main XML with a shallow real document and an unused internal entity whose quoted value contains deeply nested tag text. Request normal rendering; parser disagreement exposes literal tags to unchecked recursion.

remediationTests: Package XML containing an unused quoted DTD literal with tag text must refuse before DOM construction.
Compare admission and checked-parser outcomes for DTD/internal-subset/comment/quote cases.
Preserve supported ordinary XML documents and depth-limit boundaries.

originalCandidate.message: check_xml_depth admission.rs:794-820 ignores DocType via Ok(_); permissive parse_document parse.rs:539-542 skips <! through first > rather than DTD subset. Valid document.xml DOCTYPE internal entity containing 100000 literal <a> nesting may pass depth gate then be parsed as elements recursively. Checked validate_xml rejects DTD at parse.rs:962; admission does not. Still tracing; no execution.

findings.title: A false ZIP end record bypasses the entry-count budget
findings.summary: The preindex gate trusts the last EOCD-looking signature, while the ZIP dependency skips invalid records and may use an earlier valid directory. A small-count false record in the archive comment lets a package exceeding max_entries be indexed and processed.

severity.rationale: An input supplier can bypass an explicit resource-admission boundary with no host configuration, permitting metadata allocation and per-entry processing far beyond the caller's entry budget. Compressed/inflated byte limits remain effective; a crash is not asserted for every over-count package.
severity.changeConditions: Using one validated directory interpretation with an indexing budget prevents the mismatch; comparing the final archive count also stops later processing but cannot undo prior indexing allocation. Process limits contain impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified the bespoke last-signature count, missing actual-count upper check, and locked zip9.0.5's invalid-EOCD fallback and directory allocation. No crafted archive or runtime exhaustion was executed.

taxonomy.category: ZIP resource-limit bypass through parser disagreement

codeEvidence.label: Entry budget trusts a separate declared count
codeEvidence.explanation: Only the bespoke EOCD count is compared to max_entries before archive indexing.

codeEvidence.label: Preindex count takes the last signature without validation
codeEvidence.explanation: A later invalid EOCD-looking record in a legal archive comment can report a small count here.

codeEvidence.label: Actual archive count only checked in the opposite direction
codeEvidence.explanation: After zip chooses an earlier valid directory, a larger archive count is neither a duplicate nor compared to max_entries.

codeEvidence.label: The underlying ZIP reader resolves the actual directory
codeEvidence.explanation: Both known-offset and fallback readers use zip metadata parsing, which skips invalid EOCD candidates.

codeEvidence.label: Direct PartFs construction repeats the mismatched gate
codeEvidence.explanation: The bounded constructor indexes immediately after the same preindex count, without an actual-entry-count check.

rootCause.summary: `preindex_budget()` compares max_entries only to `declared_entry_count()`, which reads the count from the last raw EOCD signature without validating that record. `open_archive_unchecked()` lets zip9.0.5 resolve the valid directory, skipping invalid later candidates. After indexing, admit checks only whether actual count is less than the independently read count; neither it nor direct PartFs loading refuses a larger actual count. Thus the gate and consumer can disagree on the archive being bounded.

findings.remediation: Resolve and validate the EOCD/directory once with the same semantics used by the archive reader and enforce entry-count limits before allocating metadata. Also check actual archive length against max_entries immediately after opening and reject material discrepancies between validated declared and actual counts.

counterEvidence: Byte and inflated-data limits still apply; the bypass specifically concerns entry metadata/count and work.
The existing comparison detects collapsed duplicate names in the smaller-count direction.
zip's fallback behavior is valid handling of false signatures in comments; the vulnerability is the separate unvalidated resource gate.
Shared ZIP header/extent checks do not enforce max_entries.
limitations: No runtime proof or allocation measurement performed.
Practical exhaustion depends on caller limits, entry metadata size and process isolation.
validation.method: Independent parent static source/dependency control-flow review
validation.summary: A valid ZIP can contain a later EOCD-shaped record inside its comment, reporting a small count but an impossible directory offset. The custom scan takes that count. Locked zip9.0.5 rejects offsets at/past the candidate EOCD and continues to earlier candidates (format/find_central_directory.rs:100-116,163-166; read/zip_archive.rs:199-235). It then reads/indexes the earlier directory (239-316). An actual entry count above max_entries is not caught by archive.len()<declared. No local-header or CRC inconsistency is required.

findings.title: A shared font-index directory permits staging symlink overwrites
findings.summary: Native font-index saving writes to a predictable PID-based temporary file with fs::write. If an operator places the index in a directory writable by a less-trusted local user, that user can redirect a cache save to another victim-writable file.

severity.rationale: Conditional local integrity impact: the default per-user directory is ordinarily trusted. Exploitation requires a configured index parent writable by another actor, PID prediction and a victim-writable referent. Document control alone is insufficient.
severity.changeConditions: A shared writable index parent makes the path applicable. Keeping the index parent private reduces exposure; exclusive regular-file staging in a private unpredictable directory removes the write primitive.

confidence.rationale: Parent confirmed arbitrary supported index configuration, cache-miss save path, predictable name and default symlink-following write. This is conditional on explicit configuration, not a claim about any actual deployment.

codeEvidence.label: Operator can choose the index location
codeEvidence.explanation: Configured index path or parent of configured font directory determines the staging parent.

codeEvidence.label: A missing/stale font lookup saves the index
codeEvidence.explanation: Rendering a lookup not served by a current entry calls record, which saves the cache.

codeEvidence.label: Predictable temporary file is opened through fs::write
codeEvidence.explanation: A writer of a shared configured parent can plant the PID-based temp as a symlink before the default truncating write.

rootCause.summary: `font_index_path()` accepts JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or derives the cache beside the font directory. On an uncached/stale font lookup, `indexed_faces()` records and saves entries. `FontIndex::save()` replaces the extension with tsv.PID.tmp, writes using fs::write without exclusive creation/no-follow, then renames. An existing symlink in a shared configured parent redirects the truncating write before rename.

findings.remediation: Publish the font index through an unpredictable private staging directory and an exclusively created regular file held open through writing. Atomically rename only that file; refuse preexisting staging entries and document/private-parent expectations for shared configurations.

counterEvidence: Default platform location is a per-user directory; a normal document cannot change the environment or select the index path.
JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX=off disables this sink.
Only the rendering user's existing filesystem permissions are used.
Font-family path traversal is separately guarded by a single-normal-component check.
limitations: No shared-directory deployment was supplied and no file overwrite was executed.
Browser WASM has no native font-cache filesystem path.
validation.summary: README.md:907-918 documents arbitrary font/index paths and disabling the cache. The source accepts that path without requiring a private parent. Under the stated shared-parent prerequisite, a less-trusted directory writer can select a different victim-writable referent using the predictable temp entry. Real deployment evidence is not required for this conditional source path.

dataflow.summary: Configured index path -> uncached font lookup -> record/save -> predictable tsv.PID.tmp -> fs::write follows local symlink -> unrelated file overwritten
dataflow.source: Less-trusted local writer controls temporary directory entry
dataflow.outcome: Victim-writable file overwritten with font-index data.

reachability.summary: Native CLI/Python/MCP rendering reaches index saving on a cache miss. A shared writable configured index parent and a separate local writer are explicit prerequisites; ordinary document input alone is not enough.
reachability.attacker: Local user with write access to configured cache parent
preconditions: Persistent font index enabled in a parent writable by another actor.
Attacker predicts/observes PID and can create a symlink.
Selected referent is writable by renderer user.

attackPath.summary: With a native renderer configured to save its font index in a shared writable parent, a local attacker precreates the PID temporary entry as a symlink; a cache-miss lookup triggers the save.

remediationTests: A planted temporary symlink must be refused without changing its referent.
Concurrent cache saves and collisions preserve a complete regular index.
Disabled cache and default private-directory lookup keep working.

originalCandidate.originalMessage: Font-index predictable temporary is real fs::write symlink-following primitive only if attacker can write configured index parent; default is per-user data/jubarte, no document-controlled path. Checking whether docs configure shared writable location; otherwise no demonstrated crossing beyond operator config.
evidence: src/convert/font.rs:3100-3106 operator-configured index or parent(fonts)/font-index.tsv
src/convert/font.rs:3222-3227 temporary extension tsv.PID.tmp, fs::write then fs::rename
originalCandidate.notValidated: No demonstrated document-only path or confirmed lower-trust shared-cache writer; configuration prerequisites must be independently assessed before reporting.

resolved_questions.question: Full-file reads before admission
resolved_questions.resolution: MCP, Rust CLI and npm CLI read complete files before InputLimits. No standalone vulnerability absent meaningful attacker upload/root-write boundary and bounded-host-file guarantee.
